TERRAFORM PLAN COST ESTIMATE · RUNS IN YOUR BROWSER

What will this terraform apply add to the monthly AWS bill?

Paste or load a Terraform structured plan (terraform show -json) and get an approximate monthly cost delta for every create, update and delete, the biggest cost drivers, and an honest list of what could not be priced. A free, offline alternative to Infracost for the common AWS resources.

Nothing is uploaded. The file you load is read in this browser and never leaves your device. Prices come from a small bundled table of approximate us-east-1 on-demand rates dated 2026-10-03 — an estimate, not a quote.

1. Load your plan

2. Estimated monthly change

Top cost drivers

AddressActionTypeMonthly change

Every priced resource

AddressActionBeforeAfterChangeWhat it is made of

Usage-based: named, not estimated

Assumptions and exclusions

    Want this as a gate before you apply?

    Same engine, zero dependencies, one file. Fails the job when the estimated monthly delta is above a number you choose:

    terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan > plan.json
node cli.mjs estimate plan.json                          # report only
node cli.mjs estimate plan.json --max-delta 200          # exit 1 if it adds more than $200/month
node cli.mjs estimate plan.json --region eu-west-1 --json

    Get cli.mjs and engine.mjs — Node 18+, nothing to install, no network call, ever. Exit codes: 0 within budget, 1 over budget, 2 unreadable file or bad option.

    What it prices, and what it does not

    Priced: EC2 instances (with root and extra EBS volumes), EBS volumes, RDS and Aurora instances, NAT gateways, ALB/NLB/classic load balancers, Elastic IPs, EKS control planes and node groups, ElastiCache, provisioned DynamoDB, and CloudWatch alarms and dashboards. Named as usage-based and not estimated: S3, Lambda, on-demand DynamoDB, log groups and a few more. Everything else is listed as unpriced. Comparing it with the paid, multi-cloud tool? This tool vs. Infracost says where each is the right answer. Want to know what the same plan destroys rather than costs? Terraform Plan Blast Radius Check reads the same file.

    Resource typeStatus

    Common questions

    Already applied it and the bill moved? Explain the change from a Cost Explorer export with the AWS Bill Change Explainer.

    Is this an Infracost alternative?

    For one narrow job, yes: paste the JSON from terraform show -json and get an approximate monthly cost delta for the common AWS resources, with no signup, no API key and no upload. Infracost covers more clouds and uses live pricing, so it is the better tool if you need that; this is the zero-setup, offline option. See the comparison page.

    How accurate is the estimate?

    It is an approximation, not a quote. It uses a small bundled table of rounded us-east-1 on-demand list prices (dated on the page and in every report), scaled by a rough regional multiplier. It does not know your discounts, savings plans, reserved instances, spot usage or free tier, and it does not estimate usage-based charges such as data transfer, S3 storage, Lambda invocations or log ingestion.

    What happens to resources it cannot price?

    They are listed under unpriced with the reason, and the summary says the figure is not the full change. Nothing unpriced is silently counted as zero. Usage-based resources such as S3 buckets and Lambda functions are named separately.

    Is my plan uploaded anywhere?

    No. The page reads a pasted or locally loaded file in your browser and makes no network request. The CLI reads a local file and makes no network call.

    Can I fail CI when a change costs too much?

    Yes. The CLI takes --max-delta USD and exits 1 when the estimated monthly delta is above it, so it can sit between terraform plan and terraform apply. Resources it cannot price are excluded from the number the gate sees, and the output warns when that happened.

    Which file does it need?

    The structured plan JSON: terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan > plan.json. Not the text output and not the terraform plan -json stream.

vs-infracost.html.text:
← Terraform Plan Cost Estimate

This tool vs. Infracost

Different jobs. Infracost is a full cost-estimation product for infrastructure code. This is a small, offline tool for a quick monthly-cost number on the common AWS resources, with nothing to sign up for.

What each one is for

Infracost is an open-source CLI with optional hosted services. Per its own public documentation it supports multiple clouds (AWS, Azure and Google Cloud), prices resources from a maintained cloud pricing API, can estimate usage-based costs from a usage file, and integrates with pull requests and CI. It is the right choice if you need any of that.

This tool reads the JSON from terraform show -json, in a browser page or a single Node.js file, and prices a short list of common AWS resources from a small bundled table of approximate us-east-1 on-demand prices, then reports the monthly change for create, update and delete. It makes no network call, needs no account or API key, and can fail CI when the estimated delta is above a number you set.

QuestionThis toolInfracost (per its public docs)
Clouds coveredA short list of common AWS resources onlyAWS, Azure and Google Cloud, with a much larger resource list
Where prices come fromA small bundled table, dated and approximate, with a rough region multiplierA maintained cloud pricing API with live list prices
SetupNone: paste a file into a page, or run one Node fileInstall the CLI and authenticate for a pricing API key
NetworkNone. The plan never leaves your deviceCalls its pricing API to look up prices
Usage-based costsNamed, never estimatedCan be estimated from a usage file you provide
Pull-request comments and dashboardsNoYes, via its integrations and hosted offering
Budget gate in CIYes: --max-delta exits 1 over the thresholdYes, through its policy and CI features; check its docs for the current options
Resources it cannot priceListed as unpriced, never counted as zeroReported in its own output; see its docs

Use this when you want a quick, private, order-of-magnitude answer while you iterate, or you cannot or do not want to set up an API key. Use Infracost when you need accuracy across clouds, live prices, usage estimates or a team workflow. They are not exclusive: a quick offline estimate while you work and a full breakdown in the pull request answer different questions.

Statements about Infracost summarise its public documentation as best understood when this page was written and may be out of date. Check its documentation for the current feature set.

Common questions

Is this a replacement for Infracost?

No. It is a narrow, offline alternative for one job. Infracost's public documentation describes support for AWS, Azure and Google Cloud, prices pulled from a maintained cloud pricing API, usage-based estimates from a usage file, and pull-request integrations. This tool covers a short list of common AWS resources from a bundled approximate price table. If you need more clouds, live prices or a PR workflow, use Infracost.

When is this tool the better fit?

When you want a number in thirty seconds without installing anything or creating an account: paste the plan JSON into a page, or run one Node file in CI with a --max-delta threshold. It is also useful where a plan must not leave the machine and you do not want to set up an API key, because it makes no network call at all.

Is the price table live?

No. It is a small, dated table of rounded us-east-1 on-demand prices with a rough regional multiplier. Live pricing is something Infracost does and this tool deliberately does not. Treat the output as an order-of-magnitude estimate, and verify against the provider's pricing pages.

Can I use both?

Yes. A quick offline estimate while you iterate on a change, and a full multi-cloud, live-priced breakdown in the pull request, are different jobs.

Open the Terraform Plan Cost Estimate against your own plan, or check what the same plan destroys with the Blast Radius Check.
